# Commands

## relikey-agent

### relikey-agent run

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-config` | "/etc/relikey/agent.json" | configuration file |

### relikey-agent status

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-file` | "/var/lib/relikey/status.json" | the agent's status.json |
| `-max-streak` | 2 | unhealthy when this many ticks in a row end with a plan left over |
| `-max-age` | 2*time.Minute | unhealthy when the status is older than this |

### relikey-agent keygen

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-out` | "" | file for the new enrolment key (must not exist) |

### relikey-agent pin

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-cert` | "" | a PEM certificate file |

### relikey-agent statement

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-in` | "" | the statement file (kc-edge-officer-v2) |

### relikey-agent cosign

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-in` | "" | the statement file |
| `-out` | "" | file for the statement with this node's signature (must not exist) |
| `-key` | "" | this node's enrolment key file (default: enrolment_key_file in the agent's configuration) |
| `-config` | "/etc/relikey/agent.json" | the agent's configuration, for its enrolment key when -key is not given |
| `-unlock-key` | "" | this node's software unlock key file (optional: checks the statement names it) |

### relikey-agent targets

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-config` | "/etc/relikey/agent.json" | configuration file |
| `-in` | "-" | the targets as JSON, as deploy/edge/targets.py sends them; - for standard input |

## Install the shared core: `deploy/core/install.py`

```text
usage: install.py [-h] --broker-host BROKER_HOST --desk-host DESK_HOST --edge-host EDGE_HOST [--fleet-host FLEET_HOST]
                  [--fleet-officers U1,U2,U3] [--realm REALM] --root ROOT --security-officer OFFICER
                  [--edge-officer EDGE_OFFICER] [--person "First Last <e-mail>"] [--entitlement ID[:RISK]]
                  [--keyclerk-src KEYCLERK_SRC] [--keyclerk-ref KEYCLERK_REF] [--cert CERT] [--key KEY] [--port PORT]
                  [--engine ENGINE] [--lab] [--yes]

Prepare and start the ReliKey core pod (decision 0015): secrets, the front's certificate, the KeyClerk image, the
broker's realm and the desk's first records.

    python deploy/core/install.py --broker-host id.example --desk-host desk.example --edge-host edge.example         --root "Root Holder <root@example>" --officer "Officer Name <officer@example>"         --keyclerk-src ../keyclerk [--cert front.crt --key front.key] [--engine podman] [--lab]

Writes deploy/secrets/ (git-ignored; files 0600, those KeyClerk reads owned by its uid 10001), once: running it again
keeps every secret it finds there. Without --cert and --key it makes a local CA and a leaf for the three names
(front.crt holds the leaf, then the CA). With --fleet-host it also gives the fleet its page and enrolment by code
(fleet_page.py): fleet.json's admin section, once, and the page's enrol_url and pin_ca_file (the CA after the leaf).
Builds KeyClerk from its tag with KeyClerk's own Containerfile, starts the broker, sets up the realm (realm.py), then
starts the rest and prints what an edge's install.py needs: the desk's certificate pin (or the CA) and its bundle key.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --broker-host BROKER_HOST
                        the broker's name: sign-in for people and edges
  --desk-host DESK_HOST
                        the desk's name, for people
  --edge-host EDGE_HOST
                        the edge-facing name: the desk's edge routes and the mirror
  --fleet-host FLEET_HOST
                        optional: the fleet page's own name (decision 0026 point 13), signed in at the broker;
                        fleet_page.py --grant <user> admits
  --fleet-officers U1,U2,U3
                        with --fleet-host: the first officers' broker usernames, at least three; they register
                        passkeys and sign the anchor
  --realm REALM
  --root ROOT           the root holder, "First Last <e-mail>"
  --security-officer, --officer OFFICER
                        the security officer who appointed the root holder (root.officer): a core administrator, so
                        never an edge's officer
  --edge-officer EDGE_OFFICER
                        a third person, "First Last <e-mail>", to be an edge's officer (seals its ceiling): never the
                        root holder, the security officer or a privileged member
  --person "First Last <e-mail>"
                        an ordinary person to grant memberships to (repeatable): no administrator, no edge officer
  --entitlement ID[:RISK]
                        seed a catalogue entry (risk low|elevated|privileged, default elevated) and a top group
                        carrying it; an edge target names one (repeatable)
  --keyclerk-src KEYCLERK_SRC
                        a KeyClerk git repository to build v0.28.0 from
  --keyclerk-ref KEYCLERK_REF
                        lab only (with --lab): build KeyClerk from this git ref instead of the pinned tag, tagged
                        localhost/keyclerk:lab-<ref>, to try an unreleased KeyClerk
  --cert CERT           the organisation's certificate for the three names (PEM): the certificate, then the CA that
                        issued it, which enrolment codes pin
  --key KEY             its private key (PEM)
  --port PORT           the port people and edges reach the front on
  --engine ENGINE
  --lab                 add compose.lab.yaml (host network, the front on 8443)
  --yes                 start the reconciler without asking after its first dry run
```

## Register an edge at the core: `deploy/core/add_edge.py`

```text
usage: add_edge.py [-h] --edge EDGE --warpgate-url WARPGATE_URL [--engine ENGINE] [--lab]

Register one edge's Warpgate at the core's broker (decision 0010): a confidential client warpgate-<edge> with PKCE
and its one return URL, in the realm install.py set up.

    python deploy/core/add_edge.py --edge plant-a --warpgate-url https://plant-a.example:8888 [--engine podman] [--lab]

The client secret is made once into deploy/secrets/warpgate-<edge>.secret (0600, git-ignored) and handed to realm.py
on stdin; it is never printed. Carry that file to the edge, out of band, for its install.py (--sso-secret-file).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --edge EDGE
  --warpgate-url WARPGATE_URL
                        Warpgate's external URL, https://host[:port]
  --engine ENGINE
  --lab
```

## Install an edge: `deploy/edge/install.py`

```text
usage: install.py [-h] --edge EDGE --desk DESK [--desk-ca DESK_CA] [--desk-pin DESK_PIN] --bundle-key BUNDLE_KEY
                  --officer-key OFFICER_KEY [--sso-provider SSO_PROVIDER] [--engine ENGINE]
                  [--enrolment-seed-file ENROLMENT_SEED_FILE] [--re-key] [--sso-issuer SSO_ISSUER]
                  [--sso-secret-file SSO_SECRET_FILE] [--sso-client SSO_CLIENT] [--sso-ca SSO_CA]
                  [--ca-bundle CA_BUNDLE] [--warpgate-url WARPGATE_URL] [--enrol-code-file ENROL_CODE_FILE]
                  [--site-keys SITE_KEYS] [--lab]

Prepare a ReliKey edge pod: secrets, the enrolment key, Warpgate's first setup and the agent's configuration.

    python deploy/edge/install.py --edge plant-a --desk https://keyclerk.example --desk-ca desk-ca.pem         --bundle-key <64 hex, read out by the desk operator> --officer-key <64 hex> [--engine podman]         [--sso-issuer https://id.example/realms/relikey --sso-secret-file warpgate-plant-a.secret [--sso-ca front-ca.crt]] [--lab]

Writes deploy/secrets/ (git-ignored, files 0600 owned by the agent's uid 65532), runs Warpgate's unattended setup
once in its volume, and prints the enrolment key to enrol at the desk. Then: `podman compose -f deploy/edge/compose.yaml
up -d` (with `--lab`, also `-f deploy/edge/compose.lab.yaml`). Nothing here is secret-free: never commit deploy/secrets/.

With --sso-issuer, Warpgate signs people in at the core's broker (decision 0010) through the client the core made
for this edge (deploy/core/add_edge.py): authentication only. No roles claim is read; role_mappings holds one key no
identity provider sends, and Warpgate creates no users (the agent provisions them from signed leases). --sso-ca is
for a broker behind the core's local CA. SSL_CERT_FILE is process-wide in Warpgate (its rustls native roots, OpenSSL
for RDP, the S3 client for recordings), so it names a bundle of the public roots plus that CA, never the CA alone:
the public roots come from --ca-bundle, or certifi, or the host's bundle.

With --enrol-code-file (decision 0026 point 15), the edge also enrols into its fleet: the file holds the one-time code
from the fleet page (carried as a QR code or on a USB stick, never typed, never on the command line). The installer
presents this edge's enrolment key with proof of the code's secret, over TLS that trusts only the fleet's CA the
code pins (this needs Python 3.13 or later), and prints the key's fingerprint for whoever reads it to the approving
officer. Nothing is admitted until an officer approves with their passkey. To present again for an installed edge (the fleet was unreachable, say):

    python deploy/edge/install.py enrol --code-file <the code's file>

The enrolment key lives in deploy/secrets/keys/, mounted writable at /etc/relikey/keys, because a key rotation renames
the staged key over it there (#134). An edge installed before that moves its key once, then recreates the agent:

    python deploy/edge/install.py move-keys

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --edge EDGE
  --desk DESK           KeyClerk base URL (https)
  --desk-ca DESK_CA     PEM of the CA that signs the desk's certificate
  --desk-pin DESK_PIN   or: the SHA-256 pin of the desk's certificate
  --bundle-key BUNDLE_KEY
  --officer-key OFFICER_KEY
  --sso-provider SSO_PROVIDER
  --engine ENGINE
  --enrolment-seed-file ENROLMENT_SEED_FILE
                        reuse this enrolment seed (64 hex) instead of a new one
  --re-key              install over an installed edge: a new enrolment key (and admin token), so the edge is cut off
                        until it is enrolled again
  --sso-issuer SSO_ISSUER
                        the core broker's realm, https://<broker>/realms/<realm>
  --sso-secret-file SSO_SECRET_FILE
                        this edge's client secret, from the core's add_edge.py
  --sso-client SSO_CLIENT
                        the client id at the broker (default warpgate-<edge>)
  --sso-ca SSO_CA       PEM of the CA that signs the broker's certificate, when it is not a public one
  --ca-bundle CA_BUNDLE
                        the public roots to keep beside --sso-ca (default: certifi, or the host's)
  --warpgate-url WARPGATE_URL
                        the URL people reach this edge's Warpgate on, exactly as given to the core's add_edge.py: its
                        host becomes Warpgate's external_host (sign-in return URL, cookie domain)
  --enrol-code-file ENROL_CODE_FILE
                        the fleet's one-time enrolment code, in a file (QR or USB stick, never typed): the edge also
                        presents its key to its fleet (decision 0026)
  --site-keys SITE_KEYS
                        install this node with the edge's site keys (a directory made by site-keys --out on the active
                        node): the cold spare of decision 0028
  --lab                 the pod on the host network (compose.lab.yaml), to reach a core installed with --lab on the
                        same box. Never in production
```

## Apply an edge's targets to Warpgate: `deploy/edge/targets.py`

```text
usage: targets.py [-h] [--engine ENGINE] targets_file

Apply an edge's targets to its Warpgate: for each one, the role a lease names, the target, the role bound to it and
the target's pinned host key. Idempotent: run it again after any change to the file (the installation's part of
"the installation creates roles and binds them to targets"; the agent's loop only assigns roles from signed leases).

    python deploy/edge/targets.py deploy/edge/targets.yaml          # after: compose up -d

targets.yaml:
    targets:
      - name: plc-ssh                  # the target an enrolment names (enrol_edge targets[].target)
        role: plc-operators            # the role a lease for it names (enrol_edge targets[].role)
        ssh: {host: 10.0.0.5, port: 22, username: plcuser}
        host_key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."   # the target's own host key, verified out of band: required

Warpgate's admin API listens on the pod's loopback only (decision 0008), which the host cannot reach. So this checks the
file here and hands it to the agent's `targets` command inside the pod (`compose exec agent`), which applies it with the
agent's own pinned certificate and token (walk 2026-11-06, F14). The pod must be running.

Warpgate authenticates to an SSH target with its own client key; the keys it prints at the end go into the legacy
account's authorized_keys. A target without host_key is refused: Warpgate would trust whatever key answers first, and
it refuses a non-interactive first contact anyway (full-stack run, 2026-10-24).

It also writes deploy/secrets/governed-roles.json: the roles of this file, which only leases grant, as a SCIM list of
groups (RFC 7643). The agent reads it every tick and reports an account it does not manage that holds one of them,
never changing it (full-stack run 2, finding 8). The file is the edge's own source of what is governed and stays one;
with a clerk's signed catalogue in the bundle (KeyClerk 0.25.0, its decision 0025) the agent governs the union.

positional arguments:
  targets_file     the edge's targets.yaml (copy targets.example.yaml)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --engine ENGINE  podman (default) or docker, as for the edge's installer
```

## Write the enrol_edge change for the desk: `deploy/edge/enrol_change.py`

```text
usage: enrol_change.py [-h] --statement STATEMENT --targets TARGETS --name NAME [--entitlement TARGET=ENTITLEMENT]
                       [--profile {basic,assured}]

Write the enrol_edge change the desk's Edges page asks for, from the statement the officer and the edge signed and
the edge's targets file, so every field is what the two signed (rc.4 walk W2, #177: a change written by hand left out
the unlock key on the rc.3 walk, and the desk refused it as "nodes differ").

    python deploy/edge/enrol_change.py --statement st2.json --targets deploy/edge/targets.yaml \
        --name "Plant A" [--entitlement plc-ssh=plc-ssh ...] [--profile basic] > enrol.json

Root pastes enrol.json into "Enrol or rotate an edge" on the desk's Edges page and presses Review. The statement is the
one `relikey-agent cosign` wrote (st2.json): the officer's and the edge's signatures over one statement. Each target's
entitlement is the catalogue entry that grants it (the core's --entitlement); without --entitlement for a target, its
name is taken, as the install guide's example does. Nothing is sent anywhere: the desk checks the signatures itself.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --statement STATEMENT
                        the cosigned statement (relikey-agent cosign -out)
  --targets TARGETS     the edge's targets.yaml
  --name NAME           the edge's name as people see it on the desk
  --entitlement TARGET=ENTITLEMENT
                        the catalogue entry that grants a target (default: the target's name); repeatable
  --profile {basic,assured}
```

## The broker's realm: `deploy/core/realm.py` (inside the core pod)

```text
python realm.py <people.json>     (env: REALM, BROKER_URL, DESK_URL, KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME/_PASSWORD)
    python realm.py edge <edge> <Warpgate's external URL> < secret
    python realm.py vendor <alias> <issuer URL> <client id> "<display name>" < secret
    python realm.py vendor-link <username> <alias> <subject>
    python realm.py fleet <the fleet page's URL> < secret
    python realm.py fleet-grant|fleet-revoke <username>
    python realm.py setup-client      (an existing realm: add the setup client, as the bootstrap admin)
```
